newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mixed with corn options featured.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mixed with corn options featured.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed narrowly mixed with the market boosted late by small-lot short covering with action in the corn options pit generating interest, traders said.
"It wasn't quiet in here today, it was pretty active with a lot of plays," an options trader said.

In options, Continental Grain bought 1,000 December $2.70 puts and sold 500 December $3.00 puts at 18-1/2 cents, traders said. Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 800 December $2.70 calls at 7-3/4 to 8-1/4 cents and The Chicago Corp sold 400 December $2.70 calls at 7-1/2 to 7-1/8 cents, sources added.
Also Refco Inc sold 1,000 March $2.90 calls at 7-7-3/4 cents, traders said.
Corn futures sold off in early dealings despite rain-delayed harvesting of the U.S. corn crop and overall slow farmer selling.
Traders said even though farmer selling is slow, the market remains aware of a relatively large USDA-estimated 9.012 billion bushel corn crop that will come to market sooner or later.
Corn closed 3/4 cent per bushel lower to 1/2 higher, with December down 3/4 at $2.74-1/2.

USDA Monday said 45 percent of the corn crop had been harvested as of Sunday. That tally was about in line with trader expectations but sharply behind the 72 percent pace of a year ago and the 60 percent average pace.
Some traders said December corn may have been underpinned by an Internal Revenue Service memorandum recently circulated which may shift farmer selling into the 1997 tax year.

Volume was thin in the corn futures pit with Term Commodities buying one million bushels of July, traders said. Also, the Chicago Corp bought one million December while Cargill Inc and FIMAT Futures each sold one million bushels of December, traders said.

Technical traders said the key moving averages showed corn remained in a downtrend but the short term nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December closed at 23 points, into oversold territory. Traders generally view an RSI of 30 or less as indicative of an oversold market.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 62,000, down from 68,193 Monday, according to the CBOT. Corn options volume was estimated at 19,000, up from 18,725 Monday.
